event: Mount Vesuvius erupted, burying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum in volcanic ash.
The Edict of Milan was issued, granting religious tolerance to Christians in the Roman Empire.
The Western Roman Empire fell after the deposition of its last emperor, ending ancient Rome's rule in the West.
Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam, was born in Mecca.
Prophet Muhammad died, leading to the rapid expansion of the Islamic Caliphate.
Viking raiders attacked the monastery at Lindisfarne, marking the start of the Viking Age in Europe.
The Diamond Sutra, the oldest known printed book, was produced in China.
Chinese and Arab astronomers recorded a supernova that later formed the Crab Nebula.
William the Conqueror defeated King Harold at the Battle of Hastings, beginning Norman rule in England.
The University of Bologna was founded, considered the oldest university in the world.
Genghis Khan united Mongol tribes and founded the Mongol Empire.
King John of England signed the Magna Carta, limiting royal power.
Marco Polo began his famous journey to China along the Silk Road.
The Black Death plague reached Europe, killing roughly one-third of the population.
Johannes Gutenberg developed the movable-type printing press.
Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Turks, ending the Byzantine Empire.
Christopher Columbus reached the Americas, beginning sustained European contact.
Martin Luther posted his Ninety-Five Theses, sparking the Protestant Reformation.
The Aztec Empire fell to Spanish conquistadors under Hernan Cortes.
Nicolaus Copernicus published his heliocentric model of the solar system.
The British East India Company was founded.
Galileo Galilei observed Jupiter's four largest moons, supporting heliocentrism.
Galileo was tried by the Roman Inquisition for supporting heliocentrism.
The Great Fire of London destroyed much of the medieval city.
Isaac Newton published 'Principia Mathematica', founding classical mechanics.
The Kingdom of Great Britain was formed by the union of England and Scotland.
The United States declared independence from Great Britain.
The French Revolution began, overthrowing the monarchy.
Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of France.
Napoleon was defeated at the Battle of Waterloo, ending his rule.
The British Crown assumed direct control of India, beginning the British Raj.
Charles Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species'.
The American Civil War began over slavery and states' rights.
The American Civil War ended; slavery was abolished in the U.S.
The Suez Canal opened, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
Alexander Graham Bell was granted a patent for the telephone.
The Indian National Congress was founded.
Nikola Tesla developed the practical AC induction motor.
Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens.
J.J. Thomson discovered the electron.
Marie and Pierre Curie discovered radium and polonium.
The Wright brothers achieved the first powered, sustained airplane flight.
Albert Einstein published his theory of Special Relativity.
Ernest Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom.
The RMS Titanic sank on its maiden voyage.
World War I began following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
The Russian Revolution overthrew the Tsarist government.
World War I ended with the signing of the Armistice.
The Treaty of Versailles formally ended World War I.
Howard Carter discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun in Egypt.
Charles Lindbergh completed the first solo transatlantic flight.
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin.
The Wall Street Crash triggered the Great Depression.
Mahatma Gandhi led the Salt March against British colonial rule.
James Chadwick discovered the neutron.
The Summer Olympics were held in Berlin under Nazi Germany.
World War II began with Germany's invasion of Poland.
The Quit India Movement demanded an end to British rule in India.
World War II ended after atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
ENIAC, one of the first general-purpose electronic computers, was completed.
India gained independence from British rule; India and Pakistan were partitioned.
The State of Israel was established.
The People's Republic of China was founded under Mao Zedong.
The Constitution of India was adopted; the Korean War began.
Watson and Crick described the double-helix structure of DNA.
Disneyland opened in Anaheim, California.
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite.
Yuri Gagarin became the first human to journey into space.
India and China fought a border war in the Himalayas.
U.S. President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas.
India and Pakistan fought a war over Kashmir.
Apollo 11 achieved the first crewed Moon landing.
Bangladesh gained independence from Pakistan.
India conducted its first nuclear test, code-named Smiling Buddha.
The Altair 8800, an early personal computer, was released.
IBM released the IBM Personal Computer.
The TCP/IP protocol suite was standardized, forming the Internet's backbone.
A gas leak at a pesticide plant in Bhopal, India caused a major industrial disaster.
The Chernobyl nuclear disaster occurred in the Soviet Union.
The Berlin Wall fell, symbolizing the end of Cold War divisions.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web; East and West Germany reunified.
The Soviet Union officially dissolved, ending the Cold War.
Apartheid ended in South Africa with its first democratic elections.
Dolly the sheep became the first cloned mammal.
Hong Kong was handed over from British to Chinese sovereignty.
Coordinated terrorist attacks struck the World Trade Center and Pentagon on 9/11.
The Human Genome Project was completed.
NASA's Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity landed on Mars.
A global financial crisis triggered a worldwide recession.
Osama bin Laden was killed; the Arab Spring swept across the Middle East.
CERN scientists announced the discovery of the Higgs boson.
The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted by nearly 200 nations.
The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union (Brexit).
The first-ever image of a black hole was released by the Event Horizon Telescope team.
The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic.
Widespread COVID-19 vaccination campaigns rolled out across the world.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
India's Chandrayaan-3 mission achieved a successful soft landing near the Moon's south pole.
Elections were held in over 60 countries, including India, the U.S., and the EU, in the largest global election year in history.
